page: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 virtual CPUs (32 physical cores) based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is provided via 3,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. The instance demonstrates high efficiency in cryptographic and extended instruction tasks, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES-NI. Database operations and static web serving throughput are also highly rated, while memory bandwidth and single-core performance benchmarks fall within the average range.

Given its high memory density and integrated NVMe storage, the r6id.16xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for data-intensive workloads without requiring separate network-attached storage. The presence of fast local instance storage makes it highly suitable for production databases, in-memory caches, large-scale data processing, and software compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory, 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network connection. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance excels in multi-core processing, database operations, and cryptographic tasks, as evidenced by strong benchmark results in PassMark and multi-threaded decompression. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high-capacity local instance storage makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that require low-latency disk access. It is best suited for hosting large relational databases, in-memory data stores, and intensive data processing pipelines.
